Clean and merge flusurvey data tables

Source: R/merge_data.r
merge_data.Rd

Clean and merge flusurvey data tables

Usage

merge_data(
  data,
  clean = c("remove.first", "remove.bad.symptom.dates", "remove.bad.health.scores",
    "limit.season", "remove.postcodes", "n.reports", "unsuccessful.join",
    "only.symptoms"),
  min.reports = 3,
  ranges = "sample",
  age.breaks = c(18, 44, 64),
  ili.sudden.unknown = NA,
  max.band.count = Inf
)

Arguments

data

the data to merge and clean, usually the result of read_data. The surveys are joined in a fixed order (background, contact, symptom), regardless of their order in data. The last one present drives a rolling join. The result has one row per report of that survey (the symptom reports, if present), each taking the latest report of the other surveys on or before its date. For several reports from an earlier survey on the same day, the last report is used. Any other survey name gives an error.

Joining the contact and symptom surveys gives a warning. The join pairs each symptom report with the latest earlier contact report, however long before it was filed, and a contact report describes one day whereas a symptom report describes the week before it. With 'unsuccessful.join' the symptom reports without an earlier contact report are dropped, shortening episodes of illness. To link the two, extract the symptom and contact surveys separately and classify the contact reports with contact_illness.

clean

cleaning options, NULL for no cleaning, otherwise a vector of cleans to perform (by default all): - 'remove.first', whether to remove reports from the first reporting day, - 'remove.bad.symptom.dates', whether to remove bad symptom dates: symptom end of symptoms before start of symptoms, symptoms reported to have started or ended after date of report. Such dates are set to missing. Other start dates are kept as reported, and the logical column illness.ongoing.at.entry flags those before the participant's first report in the data, after any season limiting. When the first reporting day is removed, its flag is copied to reports in the same bout under the default bout boundary rules. bouts_of_illness copies the flag to the bouts. get_incidence excludes bouts with illness.ongoing.at.entry from the incidence if called with exclude = "ongoing.at.entry". - 'remove.bad.health.scores', whether to remove health scores <0 or >100 - 'limit.season', whether to limit a flu season to November -> April (when surveys are merged, the limit applies to the last survey merged: the symptom survey, if present) - 'remove.postcodes', whether to remove postcodes - 'n.reports', whether to exclude those with fewer than min.reports symptom reporting days - 'unsuccessful.join', whether to exclude those with unsuccesful joins (e.g. if symptoms are reported without a background survey present; the web site should have prevented this, but doesn't appear to have done so) - 'only.symptoms', whether to exclude those that have no report without symptoms in a season. Someone who is ill at every report may have joined or reported only because they were ill, so keeping them may introduce selection bias, most likely upwards in incidence and prevalence. Leave it out of clean for analyses that need these participants.

min.reports

minimum number of symptom reporting days per participant (ignored if 'min.reports' is not given as a cleaning option)

ranges

what to do if a number of contacts is given as a range: sample from the range ("sample"), or apply a function, given as character string (e.g., "mean")

age.breaks

a vector of the highest age (in whole years) in each age group except the last (first age group starts at 0 years of age). The last group is open-ended. The default gives the groups 0-18, 19-44, 45-64 and 65+, matching the age bands of the contact questions.

ili.sudden.unknown

how to interpret reports where sudden onset is unknown, passed to aggregate_symptoms: NA (the default) leaves ili and ili.fever missing where onset is needed to decide, 1 counts unknown onset as sudden and 0 as not sudden. The recorded onset is kept in onset.

max.band.count

the largest number of people accepted in a single age band of the household. There is no limit by default, as households in institutions such as care homes can be large. Larger counts are set to missing. nb.household is then missing too. The counts include the participant. A band ticked as present without a number counts as one person. A household with no band ticked gets a missing nb.household.

Value

a rolling-joined data table. day.of.week (1 for Monday to 7 for Sunday) is that of the report date. If the contact survey is included, contact.date is the day the contacts describe (the day before the report) and contact.day.of.week is its day of the week. Use these rather than day.of.week when analysing contacts.

Author

seb

Examples

dt <- merge_data(simulated_data[["2013"]])
#> Warning: The contact and symptom surveys are joined by report date, which pairs each symptom report with the latest earlier contact report however long before it was filed, and (with 'unsuccessful.join') drops symptom reports that have none. To link contacts to illness, extract them separately and use contact_illness().
table(dt$ili)
#> 
#>    f    t 
#> 2172   93 

## only remove each participant's first reporting day
merge_data(simulated_data[["2013"]], clean = "remove.first")
#> Warning: The contact and symptom surveys are joined by report date, which pairs each symptom report with the latest earlier contact report however long before it was filed, and (with 'unsuccessful.join') drops symptom reports that have none. To link contacts to illness, extract them separately and use contact_illness().
